title: Multiplexed-SSE reconnect state reconciliation and atomic framed tool-call preservation
creator: Avery Chen
description: Implement a reconnection and state-reconciliation strategy for multiplexed SSE connections that preserves atomic framed boundaries for function/tool calls and structured outputs. Current single-stream reconnect heuristics do not cover multiple concurrent logical streams over a single TCP connection (browser tab with multiple in-flight chats, server-to-server multiplexing). This ticket defines protocol anchors, idempotent frame markers, and server-side reconciler logic so that clients can reconnect without duplicating function-call events or producing partial structured JSON objects to downstream tool integrations.
acceptance_criteria: Clients can reconnect a multiplexed SSE connection and resume each logical stream without duplicate function-call invocations
Server emits an idempotent anchor token at the start and end of any atomic function/tool call frame; these tokens are verifiable by clients
Partial structured outputs are never delivered as completed objects to tooling integrations; incomplete frames are reconstituted or re-emitted as 'incomplete' status until healed
Automated tests cover: reconnect ordering violations, out-of-order fragment arrival, concurrent stream stall and recovery, and token collision scenarios
No regression in single-stream reconnects or non-multiplexed SSE behavior (backwards compatibility preserved)
implementation_notes: Introduce per-logical-stream monotonic sequence and an anchor hash computed over frame headers to allow idempotent deduping
Protocol: add optional HTTP response header X-RI-Multiplex: 1 when server supports server-side multiplexing; include per-event metadata 'stream_id' and 'anchor_token' in SSE data envelope
Frame format: JSON lines with 'type' (chunk|marker|function_call|end), 'seq', 'anchor' and optional 'kv' array for structured shards

Reconnect flow: client sends Last-Seq per stream in a 'X-RI-Resume' header; server computes reconciliation plan and responds with 'replay' events for missing seqs and explicit 'rebalance' markers to restart atomic frames
Server must maintain a short-lived durable replay buffer per connection for up to configured retention or until acked by client; retention TTL default 30s but configurable per customer tier
Tooling integrations: function-call frames include an 'idempotency_key' derived from model input + anchor to suppress duplicate invocation in downstream adapters
Fallback: for clients that cannot send resume headers, fall back to conservative behavior: emit 'stream-reset' and mark any outstanding tool-call as 'unknown' to avoid accidental re-exec
Metrics: expose per-stream reconnect rate, duplicate-frame suppression count, anchor-mismatch rate, and avg-replay-latency to console
qa_plan: Unit tests for anchor generation and verification (edge cases: long headers, unicode payloads)
Integration test harness simulating network partitions with multiple in-flight streams (0..10 streams) and randomized fragment drops
Load test: 10k multiplexed logical streams over 1k connections ensuring replay buffer memory stays within limits
E2E test against sample tool adapter that performs a side-effect (webhook). Use idempotency_key to assert single side-effect per logical call even with repeated replays
Compatibility test: verify older clients gracefully receive non-multiplexed stream with explanatory headers
risks: Replay buffer state explosion under high fan-out if retention not tuned; mitigated with per-customer limits and aggressive eviction
Anchor hash collisions could cause silent deduping — use strong hash and include seq to lower risk
Downstream adapters that ignore idempotency_key will still double-run; require adapter SDK changes and a rollout plan
Browser clients with HTTP/1 SSE semantics may struggle with some multiplexing patterns (we provide negotiation and fallback rules)
